findings.title: Keyboard-only players cannot complete Level 1 — puzzle pieces are non-focusable divs with no keyboard handler
findings.observed: UI state: keyboard players cannot select or swap pieces to leave the puzzle.
findings.evidence: Puzzle.jsx:66-69 renders every piece as a draggable div with click and drag handlers only; App.js:47 gates the next stage on Puzzle.onDone.
findings.expected: Checklist: essential controls support keyboard use; R-010 and R-013 require swapping pieces to advance.
reproduction_steps: Start a game using the keyboard, advance to Level 1, and tab through the puzzle screen.
Try to focus and swap two puzzle pieces; no piece is keyboard-focusable, so the mandatory level cannot be completed.

findings.title: Players see a run score unrelated to the required quiz-and-repair total — the calculation adds puzzle, lives and victory bonuses
findings.observed: Business logic: the final score includes puzzle, lives and win points beyond quiz and repairs.
findings.evidence: App.js:35 computes quiz*100 + max(0, 600 - moves*10) + fixed*150 + lives*200 + a 1000 point win bonus; Credits.jsx:44,59 posts and displays that number.
findings.expected: R-038 requires the score to equal the sum of points for quiz correct answers and correct repairs.
reproduction_steps: Complete two runs with the same quiz answers and repairs but different puzzle moves or remaining lives.
Compare the final scores: they differ despite the same required scoring inputs.

findings.title: Most cadets disappear from the leaderboard after ten submissions — the scores API unconditionally truncates results
findings.observed: Data: the 11th-ranked and lower saved cadets are never displayed.
findings.evidence: server.py:70 sorts then limits scores to 10 and Credits.jsx:62-68 renders only that response, with no pagination, count, or separate lookup for the player's score.
findings.expected: R-047, R-049, R-050 and R-051 require each submitted score to remain visible and the full leaderboard to be paged or scrolled.
reproduction_steps: Finish and save more than ten runs with different scores.
Open the leaderboard for a lower-scoring run; only the top ten are returned, without a next page.

findings.title: Players cannot tell their score failed to save or the leaderboard failed to load — both API errors are swallowed
findings.observed: UI state: a failed score save or load leaves an empty Top cadets list with no explanation.
findings.evidence: Credits.jsx:44-45 catches both POST and GET errors with empty callbacks, and the leaderboard renders the initial empty array without loading, empty, success or error messages.
findings.expected: R-042 and R-062 require plain-language score submission confirmation or failure, and R-050 requires an explicit empty state.
reproduction_steps: Finish a mission when the scores service is unavailable.
Skip or watch the credits: Top cadets is blank and there is no indication the score was not saved or way to retry.

findings.title: Skipping the credits hides every creator's name on both endings — the skip replaces the roll immediately
findings.observed: UI state: pressing Skip immediately shows the leaderboard without any creator names.
findings.evidence: Credits.jsx:11 starts the credits roll at 100vh; lines 52-53 set ended immediately on Skip, unmounting the only CREATORS list at lines 15-22.
findings.expected: R-025 requires all five named creators to appear after either ending, including the wait-free skip path.
reproduction_steps: Win or lose Level 3 and continue to credits.
Press Skip immediately; the final leaderboard appears without the five creators being displayed.

findings.title: Players can fill the public leaderboard with invented high scores — the server trusts all client-submitted results
findings.observed: Auth and access control: an arbitrary submitted score outranks genuine mission results.
findings.evidence: server.py:61-65 inserts any request with a score from 0 to 100000 and arbitrary quiz_correct, lives_left and outcome; App.js:35 calculates the real run only in the browser; GET sorts the submitted values.
findings.expected: R-038 and R-047 require leaderboard values to represent the points actually earned in a run; the checklist requires server-owned calculated scores and reliable rankings.
reproduction_steps: Submit a valid scores request containing a fabricated score above the game's achievable total, without completing a mission.
Load Top cadets; the fabricated score ranks above genuine results, with no server verification or safe player-side correction.

findings.title: Players lose their entire mission when they reload or close the page — all progress exists only in React state
findings.observed: Data: refreshing during repairs returns to the title and erases the run.
findings.evidence: App.js initializes every load at title, while puzzle order, quiz score and repair progress are local component state; there is no storage or resume path in App.js or the game screens.
findings.expected: Checklist data and persistence: user progress should survive reload; a long multi-level game must not discard a run without a recovery path.
reproduction_steps: Complete training, the puzzle and quiz and advance into repairs.
Reload the browser: the title returns and there is no way to restore the puzzle, quiz and repair progress.

findings.title: Players never see B.O.B. put the flower on the grave — the flower appears on its own after his separate animation
findings.observed: Files and media: a flower materializes on the grave without B.O.B. placing it.
findings.evidence: LoseEnding.jsx:44-46 independently scales a flower into view on the tombstone after 4.4 seconds; lines 48-50 only animate B.O.B.'s image position and rotation, without carrying or placing the flower.
findings.expected: R-022 and the user request explicitly require B.O.B. to reach Mars and place a flower at the grave.
reproduction_steps: Make three incorrect repair choices and wait through the explosion and drifting scenes.
Watch the grave scene: the flower appears independently after B.O.B. lands rather than being placed by him.

findings.title: Players on short phones lose parts of the opening screen — the centered title contents exceed a fixed, non-scrolling viewport
findings.observed: Layout: on a short phone the vertically centered title content extends beyond the viewport.
findings.evidence: App.css:28-29 fixes App and scene to 100dvh with outer overflow hidden; Title.jsx:11-12 vertically centers a single-column grid on small screens, containing a text/form column, 2rem gap and a 16rem B.O.B. image, with no scrolling.
findings.expected: R-039 and the layout checklist require primary content and controls to remain visible and reachable at phone widths.
reproduction_steps: Open the title at a narrow, short phone viewport such as 320×568.
The combined content is taller than the fixed scene; the top and bottom overflow are clipped rather than scrollable.

findings.title: The puzzle reference and completed poster appear in only one tile — the image never spans the board's grid
findings.observed: Layout: Peek and the solved poster occupy only the first grid cell, leaving the rest black.
findings.evidence: The board is a 4-column by 3-row CSS grid (App.css:79); in the peek/solved branch Puzzle.jsx:62-64 renders the image as a single grid child with no grid-column or grid-row span.
findings.expected: R-058 requires a reference image and R-013 requires the puzzle to show completion; both should show the full poster at board size.
reproduction_steps: Hold Peek while solving Level 1, or complete the puzzle.
The image is placed into one of twelve grid cells and cropped by object-cover instead of filling the board.

findings.title: Children's cadet names are published automatically without an end-of-run choice — credits immediately post the title-screen name
findings.observed: Data: finishing a mission automatically publishes the starting name without asking.
findings.evidence: Title.jsx:9 silently substitutes Alex for an empty name; App.js:36 reuses the title name; Credits.jsx:41-45 automatically posts it and has no name field or submit button; server.py:68-71 publicly returns stored names.
findings.expected: R-047 and R-061 require the player to enter and submit a 1–20 character name at the end, with empty names rejected and confirmation.
reproduction_steps: Enter a real name as the cadet name on the title screen, then finish either ending.
Open credits: it immediately posts the name to the public leaderboard, without an end-of-run choice, edit or submit control.

findings.title: Players in a webview without Web Audio cannot start with sound enabled — the sound constructor throws before navigation
findings.observed: Build and environment: Start throws before advancing when Web Audio is unavailable.
findings.evidence: sound.js:5 constructs window.AudioContext or webkitAudioContext without a feature check or catch; Title.jsx:9 calls sfx.fanfare before onStart.
findings.expected: R-027 requires sound triggers not to throw and R-001 requires Start to enter B.O.B.'s introduction.
reproduction_steps: Open the game in a browser or webview that lacks AudioContext and leave sound enabled.
Press Start; sound creation throws before onStart, so the introduction never opens. Muting first can work around it.

findings.title: Players who skip the cards face quiz questions on untaught facts — training can be bypassed with no way back
findings.observed: Business logic: skipped training leaves quiz questions about facts the player never saw.
findings.evidence: Training.jsx:54 allows 'Skip to mission' at 0/15; card explanations only render when flipped (lines 15-24). data.js:59-60 asks about CO2 removal and automatic controls, and the earlier dialogue does not teach these facts. Quiz retry only starts a new exam.
findings.expected: R-016 requires every quiz fact to have been shown in the preceding training; the user asks for Q&A after training.
reproduction_steps: At spacecraft training press Skip to mission without flipping any cards, then complete the puzzle.
Encounter a question on CO2 or autopilot; those explanations were hidden, and quiz retry has no route back to training.

findings.title: Low-vision players struggle to read primary controls and labels — the shared orange theme has insufficient contrast
findings.observed: Layout: orange and white control text has about 2.61:1 contrast, below 4.5:1.
findings.evidence: App.css uses white text on #ff7a1a buttons and B.O.B.'s orange name tag (about 2.61:1), and orange on cream panels for the small quiz progress label (about 2.39:1).
findings.expected: R-040 requires body text contrast at least 4.5:1; the checklist requires text and controls to remain legible.
reproduction_steps: Open the intro, quiz or cargo screens and inspect the orange buttons, B.O.B. name tag and small orange labels.
Players with low vision face low-contrast text on primary controls and progress labels.

findings.title: Players cannot retry a failed repair level without replaying the whole game — the ending only restarts at the title
findings.observed: UI state: after failing repairs the only replay starts the entire mission over.
findings.evidence: On the third mistake App.js routes to lose, colony and credits; the sole Play again action resets to title via go('title', INITIAL). There is no repair retry route or control.
findings.expected: The checklist requires a failed level to offer retry; a player should be able to try the repair exercise again without replaying unrelated levels.
reproduction_steps: Make three wrong repair choices and continue through the losing ending and credits.
Choose Play again: the player must repeat the introduction, puzzle, quiz and cargo before they can retry repairs.

findings_minor.title: Muted sound turns back on after a page reload — the preference is kept only in memory
findings_minor.observed: UI state: reload resets the muted toggle to sound on.
findings_minor.evidence: App.js initializes mute to false and sound.js initializes muted to false on every load; setMuted only writes the module variable and does not persist it.
findings_minor.expected: R-059 requires the mute state to survive a reload.
reproduction_steps: Mute the game using the corner button.
Reload the page; the toggle and sound are on again.

findings_minor.title: Keyboard players cannot inspect the puzzle reference — Peek only responds to mouse and touch press events
findings_minor.observed: UI state: focusing Peek and pressing Space or Enter never shows the target picture.
findings_minor.evidence: Puzzle.jsx:54-56 handles mouse and touch down/up only; the reference image is shown solely while peek is true at lines 61-64, with no key or click handler.
findings_minor.expected: R-058 requires the completed picture as a reference and the checklist requires controls to work from the keyboard.
reproduction_steps: Focus Peek with a keyboard on the Level 1 screen.
Press and hold Space or Enter; the target image is never displayed.

findings_minor.title: The leaderboard can contain blank and overlong player names — score validation checks untrimmed length against the wrong maximum
findings_minor.observed: Business logic: the scores API accepts blank-space names and names of 21–24 characters.
findings_minor.evidence: ScoreCreate.name uses only Field(min_length=1, max_length=24), and create_score inserts the payload unchanged; whitespace-only names satisfy min_length and names above the UI's 20-character limit are accepted.
findings_minor.expected: R-061 allows names of 1–20 characters and the checklist requires the server to enforce nonempty trimmed text and the same limits as the form.
reproduction_steps: POST a score with a name consisting only of spaces, or with a 21-character name.
The backend stores the record rather than reporting a name validation error.

findings_minor.title: Players cannot restart a mission from inside a level — Play again exists only after the credits
findings_minor.observed: UI state: there is no restart or quit control until after the ending and credits.
findings_minor.evidence: The App stage map exposes no quit/restart control during any level; the only onRestart is the Play again button after credits (App.js:60, Credits.jsx:69).
findings_minor.expected: R-060 requires a restart control during play that asks for confirmation and begins a fresh run.
reproduction_steps: Enter any puzzle, quiz, cargo or repair stage.
Look for a restart or quit action; the only in-app restart appears after finishing the mission.

findings_minor.title: A missing character portrait leaves a broken image on dialogue and ending screens — images have no fallback
findings_minor.observed: Layout: a failed portrait request produces a broken image instead of a labelled frame.
findings_minor.evidence: Dialogue, BobSays, colony and credits render img elements without onError handlers or labelled fallback content.
findings_minor.expected: R-041 requires a labelled fallback inside the frame when a character or colony image fails to load.
reproduction_steps: Encounter an unavailable character or colony image request during a dialogue or ending.
The image has no fallback handler or placeholder, so the portrait fails without the required labelled replacement.

findings_minor.title: Mute does not immediately silence a launch or explosion — active audio nodes continue playing
findings_minor.observed: UI state: muting during launch or explosion leaves the existing sound playing.
findings_minor.evidence: setMuted only updates a boolean checked before creating new sources; existing oscillators and noise buffer sources are neither tracked nor stopped. Launch noise lasts 3 seconds and explosion noise lasts 2.2 seconds.
findings_minor.expected: R-052 requires that no sound plays while the game is muted.
reproduction_steps: Start the launch, then press the mute toggle while the launch sound is playing.
The already-started Web Audio nodes continue until their scheduled end.

findings_minor.title: Equal-scoring cadets can change leaderboard order — scores are sorted without a tie-breaker
findings_minor.observed: Data: equal scores have no defined leaderboard tie order.
findings_minor.evidence: The leaderboard query sorts by score alone (server.py:70), without a tie-breaking sort such as created_at and id; scores have created_at and id fields at lines 51-53.
findings_minor.expected: R-051 requires a stable tie order; the leaderboard checklist requires stable sorting across pages.
reproduction_steps: Save multiple scores with the same points.
The scores query specifies no secondary order, so their relative ranking is not guaranteed across requests.

findings_minor.title: Screen-reader players cannot identify shuffle or the current mute setting — icon controls omit accessible names or state
findings_minor.observed: UI state: screen readers get an unnamed shuffle button and no mute state.
findings_minor.evidence: The icon-only shuffle button contains only the Shuffle SVG and has no accessible name; the mute button has a fixed 'Toggle sound' label without aria-pressed or another accessible state.
findings_minor.expected: The layout and interaction checklist requires icon-only buttons to have accessible labels and controls to expose their current state.
reproduction_steps: Use a screen reader on the puzzle and persistent sound controls.
The shuffle action has no name and the mute control does not announce whether sound is currently on or off.

findings_minor.title: Players cannot see how many puzzle pieces are correctly placed — the header only counts swaps
findings_minor.observed: UI state: the puzzle shows Moves but no count of pieces in their correct positions.
findings_minor.evidence: The Level 1 header displays only Moves; the order is tracked and individual correct tiles receive piece-ok styling, but the number of correctly placed pieces is never rendered.
findings_minor.expected: R-056 requires each level to show progress within it, including the number of pieces placed.
reproduction_steps: Open Level 1 and swap pieces into and out of their correct positions.
The move count changes, but no numerical placed-piece progress indicator is shown.
